summary: Cookie-header parsing must not assume a space after the separator, and must resolve percent-encoded cookie names to their canonical spelling.
reason: Neither assumption holds for this CLI's real inputs. The browser-cookie backends emit "a=1;b=2" with no space, so splitting on "; " collapses the whole header into one entry and every required-cookie lookup misses. Independently, Chrome persists several Alaska session cookies under percent-encoded names while requiredAuthCookies() looks them up canonically, so those never match even once splitting is correct. Together they made `auth login --chrome` unable to authenticate at all: login reported the required cookies missing, fell through to the live-session path, and every subsequent API call returned HTTP 406.
validated_outcome: auth_cookie_test.go fails on the pre-fix parser and passes after. Verified live end to end: login composes a 7-cookie header and validates, doctor reports reachable instead of 406, and flights search returns real fare data.
